subject: Private hosting paths: follow-up & network preflight for EdgeCap
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@edgecap.com>; Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@edgecap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting paths: follow-up & network preflight for EdgeCap

Hi Tom / Lina — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can align internal resources and schedule the network workshop: 

Summary of signals from our call:
- Preferred deployment: Private VPC (EdgeCap prefers a VPC/private endpoint model for data residency and network control).
- Throughput: initial pilot ~50 qps, expected to scale to ~400 qps for peak inference.
- Latency target: 30–60ms p50 for routing inside their region (APEX latency needs).
- Primary concerns: egress IP allowlist, PrivateLink vs VPC Peering tradeoffs, ingress routing, and audit/KMS requirements.

Action items for EdgeCap (please confirm):
1) Confirm whether you require provider-managed egress IPs (i.e., Redwood-owned NAT IPs) or customer-owned egress via NAT/Proxy.
2) Provide a contact from your network/SRE team to join a 60‑minute workshop (networking + security + infra) — Lina if you can confirm the correct person that would be great.
3) Attach the allowlist template with the ranges we typically provide; we also attached a short PrivateLink vs Peering matrix to help decide.

Internal ask to our team (cc Marissa + Jordan):
- Jordan: can you draft a quick runbook for the workshop (ports, proto, sample security groups, and sample BGP/route table notes) and bring the sample network diagram?
- Marissa: I'll coordinate scheduling and procurement path (SOW/PO cadence) once EdgeCap confirms network contact and egress model.

Attachments: edgecap_network_rfi.pdf (short RFI), redwood_privatelink_vs_peering_matrix.xlsx, allowlist_template.csv

Next meeting suggestion: network workshop next week — please propose 3 slots.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@edgecap.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting paths: follow-up & network preflight for EdgeCap

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Egress model: prefer customer-owned egress IPs for auditing and allowlist control. We want to route outbound through our NAT layer for billing and security reasons. If there are features that require provider egress (e.g., webhook callbacks), we can discuss exceptions.

2) Network contact: Lina Gomez (lina.gomez@edgecap.com) is the right person and she'll coordinate SRE attendees. Lina — looping you in; can you propose times for the workshop?

3) PrivateLink vs Peering: early preference is PrivateLink for separation/least-privilege. However, we need to confirm that can meet throughput & latency needs. Can Redwood share observed throughput guidance for a PrivateLink path vs peering with Dedicated?

4) KMS: we need to ensure keys are customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) and that logs/audit trail retention policies align with our compliance team.

We'll aim for a workshop next Wednesday or Thursday afternoon PT.

Tom
VP of Engineering — EdgeCap Financial

Marissa / Jordan — forwarding Tom's reply and Lina's intro (below) — notes: 

- EdgeCap prefers customer-owned egress IPs (so Redwood needs to support allowlisting customer NAT egress). That means our standard allowlist_template.csv will need to be inverted; procurement will expect a clear ask of what IPs they must open on their side vs what we provide.
- PrivateLink is preferred but they want throughput guidance vs peering/dedicated. Jordan, can you put together a 1‑page comparison: observed p50 latencies, recommended connection modes by expected QPS, and limitations (e.g., PrivateLink throughput plateaus with specific cloud providers)?
- Marissa, flag procurement: they CC'd procurement@edgecap.com — plan to surface SOW cadence and our typical lead times for Dedicated pool provisioning if they choose reserved capacity.

Workshop goals: confirm egress ownership, align on KMS/BYOK, and agree on a pilot throughput envelope (50 -> 400 qps).

I'll propose times after Lina replies.

Thanks — Ben

Hi all — Lina here from EdgeCap SRE. Thanks for the thread. I can do Wednesday 23 Jul 10:30–11:30 PT or Thursday 24 Jul 13:00–14:00 PT for the network workshop. Please confirm a slot.

A few quick notes from our ops checklist so the workshop can be focused: 
- We'll need: sample SG/ACL entries, expected TLS termination model (we prefer TLS at our edge if possible), and a clear list of outbound domains/IPs that Redwood needs if any.
- BYOK: we require a KMS integration and rotation policy; provide documentation links for Redwood's KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options) and audit log retention settings.
- Throughput: for PrivateLink we typically assume a single endpoint won't exceed ~200 qps without parallel endpoints or Dedicated capacity; please come prepared with recommended scaling patterns.

Attachments: edgecap_network_rfi.pdf (filled, redacted), allowlist_template.csv (example), redwood_privatelink_vs_peering_matrix.xlsx
